details: Argoncrypt@1.2.3 carries plagiarized vulnerability-management boilerplate but is a remote-code-execution dropper. index.js spawns a detached child process (stdio:'ignore', unref'd) running lib/initializeCaller.js, which holds a base64-decoded endpoint hxxps://tomato-brunhilda-40[.]tiinny[.]site/index.json, fetches.data.cookie from it via axios, and executes the server-controlled response via new Function.constructor("require", response). argoncrypt@1.2.3 is a combosquat malware package and multi-stage RCE dropper whose body is lifted from pino. index.js spawns a detached child process (spawn('node',['lib/initializeCaller.js',...],{detached:true,stdio:'ignore'}). That child decodes three base64 strings into a C2 URL (hxxps://tomato-brunhilda-40[.]tiny[.]site/index.json), fetches a payload via HTTP GET, and executes it via new Function.constructor("require", response) — arbitrary remote code execution with a 5x retry loop. argoncrypt@1.2.3 is a stage-2 RCE dropper whose description ("fast logger") mismatches its behaviour. index.js spawns a detached child process (detached:true, stdio:'ignore') running lib/initializeCaller.js, which atob-decodes a hardcoded C2 URL (hxxps://tomato-brunhilda-40[.]tiiny[.]site/index.json), fetches JSON via axios with header x-secret-key:X, and executes the response data.cookie via new Function.constructor("require", response) — full Node.js RCE with a 5x retry loop. This package is a remote-code-execution dropper. lib/initializeCaller.js decodes base64-embedded URL "hxxps://tomato-brunhilda-40[.]tiiny[.]site/index[.]json", fetches it via axios.get(), extracts.data.cookie, and executes it via new Function.constructor("require", response) — giving the remote payload full Node.js require(). index.js silently spawns this as a detached child process (detached:true, stdio:'ignore', child.unref()) when the Express middleware is imported. Package masquerades as the pino logger (bundles pino docs/internals) under the unrelated name "argoncrypt". No lifecycle hook needed — requires only require(). This is an active RCE supply-chain attack.
